title: MATH GAOKAO - 202
description: Authentic-style mathematics problems inspired by China’s Gaokao — build deeper understanding, sharper thinking, and real exam readiness.

questions.concept: Opposite angles of a cyclic quadrilateral
questions.learningObjective: Use the supplementary property of opposite angles in a cyclic quadrilateral.
questions.question: In cyclic quadrilateral \(ABCD\), \(\angle A = 85^\circ\). Find \(\angle C\).
questions.explanation: In a cyclic quadrilateral, opposite angles are supplementary, so \(\angle A+\angle C=180^\circ\). Therefore \(\angle C=180^\circ-85^\circ=95^\circ\).
questions.hint: Recall the relationship between opposite angles in a cyclic quadrilateral.

questions.concept: Exterior angle of a cyclic quadrilateral
questions.learningObjective: Apply the exterior-angle property of a cyclic quadrilateral.
questions.question: In cyclic quadrilateral \(ABCD\), side \(CD\) is extended beyond \(D\) to point \(E\). If \(\angle ABC = 110^\circ\), find the exterior angle \(\angle ADE\).
questions.explanation: Since \(ABCD\) is cyclic, \(\angle ABC+\angle CDA=180^\circ\), so \(\angle CDA=70^\circ\). The exterior angle at \(D\) is supplementary to \(\angle CDA\), hence \(\angle ADE=180^\circ-70^\circ=110^\circ\). Equivalently, an exterior angle of a cyclic quadrilateral equals the opposite interior angle.
questions.hint: Use the supplementary opposite angles and the fact that angles on a straight line sum to \(180^\circ\).

questions.concept: Angles subtended by the same chord
questions.learningObjective: Use equal angles in the same segment of a cyclic quadrilateral.
questions.question: In cyclic quadrilateral \(ABCD\), \(\angle BAC = 35^\circ\). Find \(\angle BDC\).
questions.explanation: Both \(\angle BAC\) and \(\angle BDC\) subtend the same chord \(BC\) from points \(A\) and \(D\) on the same arc. Therefore they are equal, so \(\angle BDC=\angle BAC=35^\circ\).
questions.hint: Identify the chord common to the two angles and recall the same-segment angle property.

questions.learningObjective: Determine whether a quadrilateral is cyclic from its opposite angles.
questions.question: In quadrilateral \(ABCD\), \(\angle A = 70^\circ\) and \(\angle C = 110^\circ\). Which statement is true?
questions.explanation: A quadrilateral is cyclic if and only if a pair of opposite angles are supplementary. Here \(\angle A+\angle C=70^\circ+110^\circ=180^\circ\), so the condition is satisfied. Therefore \(ABCD\) is cyclic.
questions.hint: Check whether the given opposite angles add to \(180^\circ\).

questions.learningObjective: Identify the type of cyclic quadrilateral with equal opposite sides.
questions.question: In cyclic quadrilateral \(ABCD\), \(AB=CD\) and \(BC=DA\). What is the most specific type of quadrilateral \(ABCD\)?
questions.explanation: Since both pairs of opposite sides are equal, \(ABCD\) is a parallelogram. A cyclic parallelogram must have supplementary opposite angles, and in a parallelogram opposite angles are equal, so each angle is \(90^\circ\). Therefore \(ABCD\) is a rectangle.
questions.hint: Use the fact that a parallelogram inscribed in a circle has right angles.

questions.learningObjective: Apply the right-angle property of an angle subtended by a diameter.
questions.question: Cyclic quadrilateral \(ABCD\) is inscribed in a circle, and diagonal \(AC\) is a diameter. Find \(\angle ABC\).
questions.explanation: An angle subtended by a diameter is a right angle. Since \(AC\) is a diameter, the angle \(\angle ABC\) subtends this diameter, so \(\angle ABC=90^\circ\).
questions.hint: Recall the theorem about angles in a semicircle.

questions.learningObjective: Use the property that a cyclic trapezoid is isosceles.
questions.question: In cyclic quadrilateral \(ABCD\), \(AB \parallel CD\). If \(\angle A = 75^\circ\), find \(\angle B\).
questions.explanation: A trapezoid inscribed in a circle is isosceles, so its base angles are equal. Since \(AB \parallel CD\), the angles at \(A\) and \(B\) are the base angles on base \(AB\). Thus \(\angle B=\angle A=75^\circ\).
questions.hint: Use the fact that a cyclic trapezoid must be isosceles.

questions.concept: Opposite angles of a cyclic quadrilateral with variables
questions.learningObjective: Solve for an unknown using the supplementary opposite-angle property.
questions.question: In cyclic quadrilateral \(ABCD\), \(\angle A=(2x+10)^\circ\) and \(\angle C=(3x-20)^\circ\). Find \(x\).
questions.explanation: Opposite angles in a cyclic quadrilateral are supplementary, so \((2x+10)+(3x-20)=180\). Simplifying gives \(5x-10=180\), hence \(5x=190\), and \(x=38\).
questions.hint: Set the sum of the opposite angles equal to \(180^\circ\).

questions.concept: Angle chasing in a cyclic quadrilateral
questions.learningObjective: Use arcs and inscribed angles to find an unknown angle.
questions.question: In cyclic quadrilateral \(ABCD\), \(\angle ADB=30^\circ\), \(\angle DBC=40^\circ\), and \(\angle BCD=100^\circ\). Find \(\angle DAB\).
questions.explanation: Let the arcs \(AB, BC, CD, DA\) have measures \(x,y,z,w\). From \(\angle ADB=30^\circ\), \(x=60^\circ\). From \(\angle DBC=40^\circ\), \(z=80^\circ\). Since \(\angle BCD=100^\circ\), the arc \(BD\) not containing \(C\) has measure \(200^\circ\), so \(x+w=200^\circ\), giving \(w=140^\circ\). Then \(y=360^\circ-(60^\circ+80^\circ+140^\circ)=80^\circ\). Finally, \(\angle DAB\) subtends arc \(DB\) not containing \(A\), whose measure is \(z+y=80^\circ+80^\circ=160^\circ\). Hence \(\angle DAB=80^\circ\).
questions.hint: Convert the given inscribed angles to arc measures and use the total \(360^\circ\) around the circle.

questions.learningObjective: Use Ptolemy's theorem to find the product of the diagonals of a cyclic quadrilateral.
questions.question: In cyclic quadrilateral \(ABCD\), \(AB=3\), \(BC=4\), \(CD=5\), and \(DA=6\). Find \(AC\cdot BD\).
questions.explanation: By Ptolemy's theorem for a cyclic quadrilateral, \(AC\cdot BD=AB\cdot CD+BC\cdot DA\). Substituting the given side lengths gives \(AC\cdot BD=3\cdot5+4\cdot6=15+24=39\).
questions.hint: Use Ptolemy's theorem, which relates the diagonals to the four sides.
